newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB rallies on hopes for digital start.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB rallies on hopes for digital start.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc shook off their early weakness by mid-morning on Wednesday on confirmation that the company plans an autumn launch of digital satallite television in the UK, traders said.
The news helped counter an initial disappointment with the company's first-half figures showing pre-tax profit no better than analysts had expected.
The stock was up 16p at 609 by 1034 GMT, after recovering from a 10p drop in early trading.
"They came down a bit on the results which were in line with expectations," one trader said. "But people still fancy them with the digital TV business going ahead."

BSkyB said today it planned to launch a 200-channel digital satellite television service in the UK on a pay-per-view basis this autumn, in a venture announced last week with Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc.
